question: Should memory-wiki intentionally narrow ChatGPT timestamp strings from all finite `Number()`-coercible inputs to signed canonical decimal syntax, including rejecting exponent and whitespace-padded forms?
rationale: The patch prevents silent coercion of malformed values, but it also changes the import compatibility contract for previously accepted finite strings; source and tests alone do not establish which legacy forms should remain supported.

options.title: Adopt canonical decimal strings
options.body: Confirm that ChatGPT import accepts only finite numbers and signed canonical decimal strings, then require live proof for that contract.

options.title: Preserve compatible numeric spellings
options.body: Keep accepting documented finite numeric string forms while adding a narrower guard that rejects trailing or embedded junk.

options.title: Pause for importer contract review
options.body: Hold the PR until the memory-wiki owner defines the supported timestamp grammar and upgrade expectations.

recommendation.title: Adopt canonical decimal strings
recommendation.body: Confirm that ChatGPT import accepts only finite numbers and signed canonical decimal strings, then require live proof for that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available adjacent routing candidate for the memory-wiki import surface.
